name: Bats

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Bats (bats1242).

notes: Research. Bats (Tsova-Tush) is a Nakh (Northeast Caucasian) language written in the Georgian Mkhedruli script supplemented by extra letters. The 33 standard Georgian letters take their usual phonemic values, including the ejective series; added signs write the schwa ჷ (ə), the pharyngeal ჺ (ʕ), the glottal stop ჸ (ʔ) and ჶ (f). Bats has a much larger consonant inventory than Georgian -- including pharyngealized consonants, additional uvulars, a voiceless-lateral series and nasalized vowels -- much of which is written with digraphs and diacritic combinations not resolved by this single-symbol map; those distinctions are left under-encoded, so a substantial PER floor is expected. Grapheme table checked against Holisky & Gagua (1994): no discrepancy found. Stress: Holisky & Gagua (1994) describe Bats stress as weak and dynamic but gravitating toward the word-initial syllable, occasionally shifting under morphological conditions the `stress` schema cannot express; `default_position=1` encodes the unmarked initial-stress tendency as an approximation, and the morphologically-conditioned shifts are a documented gap rather than silently wrong.
